title: Coefficient four with explicit loss (359/25)n^(4/5)

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. Let L(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee.leading. Let R(n) be the sum of the monomials in guarantee.remainder.terms, each coefficient times n^exponent*(log2 n)^log_exponent*(log2 log2 n)^loglog_exponent; an empty sum is zero. There exists N such that C_B2(f_n)>=L(n)-R(n) for every integer n>=N. All remainder coefficients are the exact declared constants. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The single total polynomial-time language defined in proof.md: f_0=0. For n>=1 choose the least positive integer s with s^5>=4*n^3 and the least prime k>s; return 0 if k>=n. Otherwise the last k input bits encode a monic degree-k binary polynomial h and the first N=n-k bits are data. In F_2[Z]/(h), pad the data into r=ceil(N/k) blocks X_j, put t=ceil(sqrt(r)) and u_j=r+1-j, and output the constant coefficient of the degree-t elementary symmetric sum on X_j^(2^u_j-1). This ring evaluator is defined even for reducible h. Its empty-witness verifier accepts exactly its yes inputs.","guarantee":{"kind":"eventual_lower_bound","leading":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"remainder":{"kind":"explicit","terms":[{"coefficient":{"denominator":"25","numerator":"359"},"exponent":{"denominator":"5","numerator":"4"},"log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}}]}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one fixed total uniform polynomial-time family, hence in NP with witness bound zero, there exists an integer n_0 such that for every integer actual input length n>=n_0, C_B2(f_n)>=4*n-(359/25)*n^(4/5) in the full Li\u2013Yang B2 model, and hence liminf C_B2(f_n)/n>=4.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v2"}

claims: For a prime-degree binary field K of dimension k, integers r>=1 and t=ceil(sqrt(r)), and any nonzero binary-linear functional pi on K, the block polynomial pi(Sym_r^t(X_j^(2^(r+1-j)-1))) is nonconstant on every affine subspace of K^r of binary dimension greater than k*t+r*(r+1)/2, as proved in proof.md.

If a Boolean function on N bits is nonconstant on every affine subspace of dimension d, with integers 1<=d<=N, then every exact single-output circuit for it in the full B2 model has at least 4*N-10*d gates, as proved in proof.md.
